fields.position: Evolve reward objectives under fixed dynamics and compare trained-policy cross-fitness profiles; the local scope is paper mathematics and selection only.
fields.tradeoff: AlphaEvolve evolves candidate programs under a human-fixed evaluator. Habitats changes rewards and evaluation coordinates; cross-generation profiles are not a fixed benchmark. Neither local entry establishes full discovery capability.

fields.title: Objective discovery and fixed-objective program search use different evaluation coordinates
fields.body: Separate the evolutionary object from its evaluator. AlphaEvolve changes programs under a fixed human objective; Habitats changes rewards under fixed dynamics and trains new policies, using policy-by-reward profiles for mastery and transfer. SQ/BD use within-generation coordinates. GC grounds, quantizes and deduplicates within each generation before summing, not counting unique skills across time. Numerical quality/diversity does not replace real Planner/Mutator or RL. The pinned source and paper normalize differently, so the chosen convention must be explicit. The hour-scale CPU/H100 and multi-model campaign remains terminally not reproduced; a CPU kernel neither reopens it nor qualifies for Evolve.

fields.question: Why are Habitats and AlphaEvolve different forms of code evolution?
fields.answer: AlphaEvolve evolves programs under a human-fixed task and evaluator. Habitats fixes environment dynamics but evolves reward objectives, trains policies and compares policy-by-reward profiles. Their changing objects and evaluation coordinates differ; code counts do not establish a capability winner.
fields.example: Teaching example: improving matrix multiplication under one evaluator keeps the objective fixed; discovering clearing-versus-collecting objectives in one card environment changes objectives. Both still require executed validation.
